Status.note: Status stays construction. Basin Electric told the North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality in a letter dated January 21, 2026 that construction began on January 8, 2026. A Basin Electric news release from May 2026 and a Minot Daily News article from May 2026 report the groundbreaking. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 still shows regulatory approvals pending, which looks out of date because it predates these documents.

Capacity (MW).note: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists plant 69071 with a combustion turbine of 496.0 MW and a steam turbine of 263.0 MW for this block, so 759.0 MW nameplate. The air permit at https://ceris.deq.nd.gov/ext/ncore/downloadpdf/-6052959693102246591 and the Basin Electric release at https://www.basinelectric.com/News-Center/news-releases/Basin-Electric-breaks-ground-on-historic-generation-facility both say about 745 MW per unit, and the Southwest Power Pool queue shows 760 MW. The permit and release do not say whether 745 is nameplate.

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note: The final air permit to construct ACP-18273 version 1.0 from December 2025 lists a Mitsubishi 1x1 M501JAC natural gas combined cycle combustion turbine with a duct burner for each block.

Start year.note: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 gives a planned operation of February 2029 for this block. The human adds a new scheduled event with 2029 as Event Year and 2026 as Source Year.

qa.question: Does Bison need extra units for the Sierra Club CA1 and CA2 rows?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) lists each block as a 496 MW combustion turbine plus a 263 MW steam turbine, generators CA1 and CT1 for block one and CA2 and CT2 for block two. The CA rows are the steam turbine halves of the two blocks that GEM holds as units 1 and 2.
qa.recommendation: Add no new units. Leave units 1 and 2 as combined cycle blocks.
qa.note: I did not cite the Sierra Club list. The Southwest Power Pool queue entries GEN-2024-081 and GEN-2024-082 were not downloaded in this pass.

qa.question: Should unit capacity change from 745 MW to 759 MW?
qa.finding: The EIA table gives 759.0 MW nameplate per block, while the permit at https://ceris.deq.nd.gov/ext/ncore/downloadpdf/-6052959693102246591 and Basin Electric's release at https://www.basinelectric.com/News-Center/news-releases/Basin-Electric-breaks-ground-on-historic-generation-facility say about 745 MW per unit.
qa.recommendation: Keep 759 MW if you accept the EIA nameplate over the company's round figure. Otherwise leave 745 MW.
